Chapter 01 · My foundation

My learning brings business, software engineering and data modelling together.

I began with a Bachelor of Arts in Economics, Law and Politics at Rhodes University. Studying organisations through economic, legal and political perspectives shaped how I understand decisions and their wider context. My Postgraduate Diploma in Enterprise Management, also at Rhodes, connected that foundation to how organisations are run.

In 2026, I studied Software Engineering at Hyperion Development. It added a technical perspective through programming and software development, complementing my business studies and my interest in business intelligence.

I continue to build on this foundation through Udemy learning in data modelling and related areas, including financial modelling and ERP implementation. This helps me connect business questions to the way data and systems are structured.

Chapter 02 · My delivery experience

I oversee programme delivery and reporting for a programme budgeted at R9 million.

I have also improved how programme information is organised and processed, making it more useful for analysis and reporting.

How I structure programme data

PROGRAMMEPK programme_idprogramme_name
1:N
ACTIVITYPK activity_idFK programme_id
1:N
RESULTPK result_idFK activity_idindicator · value

One programme can contain many activities, and each activity can link to multiple result records. Primary keys identify records; foreign keys preserve the relationships so reporting can group results by programme without repeating programme details.PK = primary key · FK = foreign key · 1:N = one to many

Chapter 04 · My financial modelling

I connect operational drivers to financial forecasts.

I am developing financial models that link delivery plans to costs. Volumes, unit rates, timing and scenarios show how changes in assumptions affect the forecast and expected spend.

My financial workbook brings assumptions, activity plans, actuals and forecast outputs together.

How the forecast is built

Forecast to completeRemaining activity volume × unit rateEstimate future cost from the work still planned and its cost per activity.
Estimate at completionEligible actuals to date + forecast to completeCombine recognized spend through the reporting cut off with the cost still expected.
Budget positionApproved budget − estimate at completionPositive means forecast headroom. Negative signals a potential overspend to review.

Chapter 05 · My direction

Business intelligence is where I am taking this work.

I have already worked on improving data handling, processing, analytics and visualisation. In project management, I have used information to support decisions about delivery, risks and finances. I am building on that experience through financial modelling and practical BI work, with a clear focus on a career in business intelligence.

02 · Data cleaning and SQL

Sales data cleaning project

An Excel data preparation exercise using 240 deliberately inconsistent synthetic sales records and equivalent SQL examples.

  • Raw source tab preserves mixed casing, formats, missing values and duplicates
  • Standardized fields and parsed amount staging
  • Duplicate, missing, invalid and unmapped value checks
  • Exception queue, SQL patterns, field definitions and quality summary
Excel workbook · 240 synthetic sales records

Clean, validate, review

Illustrative logic pipeline
  1. 01Preserve the raw sourceKeep source rows unchanged for traceability
  2. 02Standardise fieldsNormalize labels and parse dates, quantities and amounts
  3. 03Run quality checksIdentify duplicates, blanks, invalid values and unmapped labels
  4. 04Separate ready and review rowsPass qualified records forward and retain exceptions
Before and after · raw rows to controlled staging

Only unique rows with valid dates, amounts, quantities and mapped values enter qualified sales totals. Every rejected row remains visible with its issue flags.

What this helps decideWhich sales records are ready for reporting and which need correction or investigation first.

03 · Financial modelling

Moya Trail Gear three-statement model

I built an integrated monthly model for a fictional South African outdoor retailer. It combines three months of actual results with a nine-month forecast for 2026.

  • Preserved raw journal entries alongside standardized entries and an opening trial balance
  • Forecast revenue, cost of sales, expenses, tax and net income
  • Linked working capital, equipment and debt schedules to the three statements
  • Drivers for sales growth, cash and credit mix, inventory cover, operating costs and borrowing
  • Monthly balance sheet, cash flow and schedule checks
My Excel model · fictional practice data

Moya Trail Gear · 2026

How the model flows
  1. 01Prepare the sourceRetain raw entries, standardize accounts and reconcile opening balances
  2. 02Set forecast driversChange growth, sales mix, cost rates and operating assumptions
  3. 03Build supporting schedulesCalculate collections, inventory, supplier payments, equipment and debt
  4. 04Link and check the statementsConnect income, balance sheet and cash flow, then review reconciliations
Illustrative model outputs · 2026
R992,022Full-year revenue
R130,577Full-year net income
R133,923December cash
PASSMonthly model checks
Selected formulas from the workbook
Income Statement · E5Forecast revenue from growth=D5*(1+Assumptions!B4)
Income Statement · E6Cost of sales from revenue=E5*Assumptions!B7
Cash Flow · E23Closing cash=E22+E21
Balance Sheet · E23Assets less liabilities and equity=E11-E22

Forecast drivers include 8%, 5% and 3% monthly growth phases, a 42% cost-of-sales rate, 60% cash sales, 40% credit sales and 1.5 months of inventory cover. The figures are fictional practice results.

What this helps decideHow sales, costs, working capital and investment assumptions affect profit, borrowing and cash through the year.

Python sales data quality pipeline

A small pandas example that prepares inconsistent sales records for analysis and keeps rejected rows visible for review.

  • Reads a raw CSV without overwriting the source
  • Standardises IDs, customer names, regions and product names
  • Parses mixed dates, quantities and Rand amounts
  • Separates qualified records from rows with issue flags
Python · pandas · illustrative project

Prepare, validate, review

What the run produced
22Raw rows
12Qualified

The script records its rules, preserves the raw file, and exports a clean dataset, exception list and quality summary. All sales records are synthetic.

Process: raw CSV → standardise fields → validate records → export qualified data and exceptions.

What this helps decideWhether a new source file is reliable enough to analyse, or needs data owner review before use.
